To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) for a metallic cavity the charge relaxation resistance is universal at the charge degeneracies and equals the unit resistance, (ii) the weak tunneling limit of the charge relaxation resistance can be mapped to a Kondo model with a non-Fermi liquid fixed point, (iii) the charge degenerancies are robust in the presence of channel asymmetry, and (iv) the charge degenerate points are robust in the two channel limit in the presence of backscattering asymmetry.

the charge relaxation resistance is universal in the vicinity of charge degeneracy and at low frequencies for a metallic cavity, that this universality can be understood in terms of the interplay between cross mode mixing and the Kondo effect, and that the weak tunneling limit can be mapped onto the strong tunneling limit by a simple transformation.

the charge relaxation resistance of a multichannel RC quantum dot circuit, in the low frequency ac regime, is universal for a metallic system, and equals the resistance quantum {R}_{q}, when the dot is tuned to a charge degeneracy point and the tunneling rates are weak.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the strongly correlated dynamics of multichannel quantum circuits, which is of interest for the emerging field of quantum information processing.
the dynamics of strongly correlated quantum RC circuits in the presence of dissipation.
the dynamics in a multichamber quantum RC circuit, with a special focus on the strongly correlated regime, where the system is described as a multichannel Kondo model, or a Luttinger liquid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in a multichamber quantum RC circuit, {R}_{q}, in the limit of weak tunneling, is a function of the interchannel asymmetries and the number of channels, but is independent of the details of the tunneling amplitudes.
the quantum RC circuit with a metallic dot is an ideal system to study dissipation effects in quantum transport.
in the quantum RC circuit the charge relaxation resistance is universal, but only for the special case of a metallic cavity.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the interplay between the number of channels, the interchannel coupling, and the asymmetry of the backscattering can be used to engineer the transport properties of the system, and to tune it between the two limiting cases of weak tunneling and perfect transmission.

the charge relaxation resistance in a multichanel quantum RC circuit can be tuned to the universal unit of quantum resistance by adjusting the interchannel coupling, the tunnel coupling and the temperature, and is therefore a promising platform for quantum metrology applications.
dissipation is a crucial ingredient for the understanding of transport in multichannel systems.
